text:
carla: Noticing a new pattern in us-central: tiny training pods (0.125 GPU) scheduled heavily on the same rack, starving other racks -> fragmentation and then evictions when batch attach fails. Started ~02:30 UTC after the affinity tweak rollback.
ev an: saw a spike in podPending and evict counts. Telemetry: scheduling_affinity_score median jumped from 0.6 -> 0.92 for rack A.
tess: quick dump of scheduler decisions around one example: 
```
I0410 02:31:22 scheduler.go:471] Evaluate pod tiny-job-58 on node gpu-node-7: affinity_score=0.95 (rack=A), pack_score=0.81, final_score=1.76
I0410 02:31:22 attach-controller.go:88] Attach failed: insufficient allocatable gpus on gpu-node-7: wanted=0.125 available=0.0
I0410 02:31:23 scheduler.go:521] Reschedule pod tiny-job-58
```
carla: So affinity_score is dominating pack_score, looks like normalization dropped. We recently normalized soft-affinity by node.cpu_capacity in the refactor; maybe CPU label missing on some nodes causes extremely high score.
ev an: Pulled node metadata: gpu-node-7 missing `node.k8s/cores` label due to kubelet relabel changes. Affinity code divides by cores -> divide-by-zero guard returns +Inf -> clamp to large int. That would explain the huge affinity bias.
tess: Nice catch. Quick patch idea: change normalization to use `max(1, cores)` and add unit test. I'll open a PR.
carla: For immediate relief: 1) set `scheduler.alpha/soft-affinity-weight=0.0` via rollout config for us-central for 10 mins to let pending pods spread; 2) ops spin up 10 extra warmpool tiny slots across other racks.
ops-runner: I can add warmpool nodes to racks B/C now. Running: `ops-runner scale warmpool --region us-central --count 10 --size tiny`
ops-runner: done. Also temporarily adjusted eviction grace to 45s for training ns.
infra-bot: deploy job started: scheduler/normalize-guardfix #909 -> staging (us-central)
ev an: PR opened: https://git.redwood/scheduler/pull/909 - includes guard, tests, and a telemetry alert when normalization factor > 100.
tess: Canary in staging looks clean; nodes with missing cores now treated as 1 and affinity score sane. Rolling to prod in 7m.
carla: After prod rollout, run requeue controller to avoid mass-deletes: `kubectl get pods -n training --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o name | xargs -n1 -P10 kubectl patch -p '{"spec": {"priority": 0}}'` (poke without deleting).
ev an: Be cautious with that patch approach, might trigger admission. I'll implement a controller that emits a benign annotation to force re-evaluation.
ops-runner: Prod rollout done. Early telemetry shows pending pods decreasing and rack distribution flattening.
carla: Action items: 1) backfill node labels for cores during node bootstrap, 2) add normalization guard + tests (tess), 3) ops playbook for warmpool rapid scale (ops-runner), 4) safer requeue controller (evan). I'll own the postmortem writeup.
tess: Thanks all. Will follow up with PR link and release notes. :thumbsup:
